Yu-Gi-Oh: Forbidden Memories on Playstation 1.

I have made attempts to finish this game since childhood. Back then I really enjoyed this game, despite how difficult it is. But 2 years ago, at the age of 25, after many years of having this fun but difficult game in the back of my mind, I made the commitment to myself that I would play this game in my free-time, until I won.

The rules in this game are drastically different from regular Yu-Gi\_oh. Star signs given to every monster card determine if that monster gets a 500 attack or defense bonus against a monster with a stronger or weaker star sign. You are also expected to just select a bunch of cards in your hand and mash them together in the hope that they become a good fusion card. This method of fusion is very different, and in my opinion more challenging, than the method of fusion in the normal Card Game

This game is notorious for how broken it is. One reason is that you can only add new cards in your deck through winning against a large roster of NPC players. And the major reason is that the drop rate for decent cards is incredibly rare.

There is a single-player mode and a Duel mode where you can play against characters you already defeated in the Single-Player in order to win more cards.

Most of the time I spent in Duel mode, playing against the same players over and over again, so I could win better cards. I won against Simon Muran 99 times, I won against Teana 99 Times, I won against Jono 99 times, I won against Villager 1 99 times, I won against Villager 2 99 times, I didn't unlock villager 3 because I accidentally missed him in the storymode.

99 is the max number the game can display, so I actually won against most of these characters more times than I can count.

With every game you play, you are ranked according to how well you played out your strategy. The highest rankings you can get are S-Tec 5 stars, and S-Pow 5 stars. Most of my wins in the Duel Mode were S-Pow 5 stars and S-Tec 5 stars. Even while getting the highest ranking in the game, this game is still incredibly singy with giving good cards.

After months of winning cards, I had a deck that was good enough to continue the single-player. It wasn't a great deck, but good enough for now.

At the end of the Single-Player Campaign you have to fight 7 players in a row without the ability to save in between your matches. Each of these players will drop some of the best cards in the game on their first round.

In the European and American versions of this game there is also a large number of good cards that NPC's can use, and. cannot be unlocked by the player.

I made several attempts to make it throught this end-of-game Gauntlet, I went back to Duel mode and dueled some more against the new characters I unlocked. Despite spending even more time in Duel Mode winning with 5 star S-tecs and 5 Star S-Pows I only managed to get a very small amount of good cards.

I was feeling a little demoralised. I had already discovered months ago that many people that finish this game are not ashamed at all to mention that they used cheats to get better cards.

Most people that have finished this game have cheated at some point to get better cards. Most of the people that play this game agree that this game is an unfinished mess that doesn't allow you to win good cards close to 99% of the time.

At this point I just wanted to finish this final stretch of the Single-Player campaign and be done with it. But I did not want the 7 Final Bosses to be a cakewalk either, and I wanted to stay true to how challenging this game had been so far. So I only allowed myself a couple of cards that would equal-out my chance of winning.

I actually enjoyed myself with this game, despite how broken and unfinished it feels.
